The State of Some Data

Author

Dan Hill et. al., IPRC

Published

February 20, 2026

1 Spending Authorization

1.1 LSA Counts

Here we have annual data on number of Spending Authorizations submitted:

  • The number submitted yearly (in a given year).
  • The change (and % change) in the number submitted compared to the previous year.
  • Total cumulative submitted since the beginning of the settlement.

Note that FY 2026 is only about half over, so these numbers will undoubtedly rise over the coming months.

1.2 Gov’t Counts

Here we have annual data on the number of local governments submitting spending authorizations:

  • The number submitting yearly (in a given year).
  • The change (and % change) in the total number of governments submitting over the previous year.
  • The total cumulative number of local governments that have submitted any spending authorizations since the beginning of the settlement.

1.3 Unique Strategy Counts

Here we have annual data on the number of unique strategies authorized:

  • The number of unique strategies authorized yearly (in a given year).
  • The change (and % change) in the total number of unique strategies funded over the previous year.
  • The total cumulative number of unique strategies authorized since the beginning of the settlement.

2 Funding

2.1 Total Spent

Here we have data on the total amount of settlement funds spent on strategies:

  • The total amount spent yearly.
  • The change (and % change) in the amount spent from the previous year to the current year.
  • The total cumulative amount spent since the beginning of the settlement.

2.2 Gov’ts Funding

Here we look at the total number of local governments spending settlement funds:

  • The total number of governments funding strategies yearly.
  • The change (and % change) in the total number of governments funding strategies over the previous year.
  • The total cumulative number of unique local governments that have funded any strategies since the beginning of the settlemnet.

2.3 Total Strategies

Here we have data on the total number of strategies funded anually:

  • The total number funded yearly.
  • The change (and % change) in the number of strategies funded from the previous year.

Note there is no meaningful “cumulative” value; any given government may fund the same program multiple years in a row, complicating this as a measure.

2.4 Unique Strategies

Here we have data about the number of unique strategies funded anually:

  • The total number of unique strategies funded yearly (in a given year).
  • The change (and % change) in the number of unique strategies funded over the previous year.
  • The cumulative number of unique strategies funded since the beginning of the settlement.
